definitions.start_rule: client_start_date (Jira): for issues created before 1 Jun 2026, the issue due date, or the issue created date + 4 days when no due date is set; for issues created from 1 Jun 2026, the Pipedrive won date. won_clients_master falls back to the won date when no Jira start exists and labels it 'Pipedrive Fallback'; fallback dates are not confirmed starts and are excluded from starts and cohorts.

milestones.uc: property_uc_date: the latest currently valid Under Contract date, falling back to the first. Not immutable history: a contract that falls through can move or clear it.
milestones.pi: property_passed_inspection_date: date the property passed inspection.
milestones.closed: property_closed_date: the closing milestone. Dates after the data date are scheduled closings and are not counted as closed in this build.
milestones.refund: client_refunded_date: date the Jira status last changed to Refunded (a status proxy, not a verified refund transaction).

definitions.henry: HENRY = total out-of-pocket capital (Jira total_oop) of $225,000 or less. Clients without a total_oop value are 'unknown', not 'not HENRY'.
definitions.cash: Modeled contractual cash (client_cash_forecast), not verified receipts or accounting revenue. Paid In Full: 100% assumed collected in the won month. Split Pay: 50% assumed collected in the won month and 50% at property close; unclosed split pay carries 50% modeled outstanding. Refund-excluded amounts zero the whole engagement when the Jira status is Refunded.

form.measures: down payment + closing costs + renovation + furniture + amenities: all-in capital, not the purchase price
form.rule: upper end of the selected range (the interim rule, also being carried into Jira's budget field)

terms.unit: One STR Search pipeline deal, normally one booked strategy call
terms.source: pipedrive_reporting_base, keep = true, lost reason not Test Lead / Duplicate
terms.calc: Count of in-scope deals. Status today: won (won date set), lost or open.

terms.unit: One won STR Search deal; a client who buys twice has two
terms.source: won_clients_master (one row per won deal, refunds and repeats included)
terms.calc: Count of won deals. Booked value = the deal value sales entered, not cash.

terms.date: Deal created date (the cohort) and won date
terms.calc: Won ÷ deals created. 'Within N days' counts only deals created at least N days before the data date.

terms.source: pipedrive_reporting_base pd_qualified flag (the reporting layer's qualification rule)
terms.calc: Share of in-scope deals with pd_qualified = 1.

terms.date: Created date → won or lost date
terms.calc: Won date − created date; lost date − created date. Medians use pandas' linear interpolation.
Data date − created date, for deals neither won nor lost.

terms.source: utm_source on the deal (cleaned: ig/instagram → Instagram, fb → Facebook)
terms.calc: As recorded; blank = Unknown. Filled on a minority of deals, so channel rates describe tagged deals only.
As recorded; blank = Not filled.
Legacy or New Client Experience (onboarding before the sale, from 27 May 2026); blank = Not tagged.
Jira issues whose status is in the signed-up list; prospects (New Clients, Onboarding Completed, Services Declined) are not.
Inactive = Paused, Refunded or Additional Service; Active = the rest of signed-up, including clients who already bought; Hunting = Client Start and 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 Weeks.

terms.date: The start of the acquisition clock
terms.calc: Issues created before 1 Jun 2026: the due date (kickoff), or created date + 4 days; from 1 Jun 2026: the Pipedrive won date.
A won deal whose start comes from Jira. Pipedrive-fallback starts (won date only) are left out of every duration and cohort.
The latest currently valid Under Contract date (falls back to the first). A contract that fell through can move or clear it.
Closing date on or before the data date (later dates are scheduled, not closed). Completed purchase (status first) = CLOSED or post-close status, or a closing recorded on a contract.

terms.term: Days to UC / UC to close
terms.unit: Confirmed starts that reached the milestone
terms.calc: UC date − client start date; closing date − UC date. Averages and medians cover only clients who reached the milestone.

terms.date: Client start date (or won date on the won-date clock)
terms.calc: SUM(uc_within_N × eligible_N) ÷ SUM(eligible_N): a client counts only once N days have passed since the start (eligible). 'Maturing' = some clients have not had N days yet.
Day by which half of the clients reached the milestone, counting clients still waiting (hunting, paused, refunded) until the data date. Assumes they progress as earlier clients did.

terms.date: Client start → the day after the data date
terms.calc: Every hunting search counts as going Under Contract the day after the data date; pooled once per search with the recorded durations of every other search. A floor for the hunting clients, not a forecast.
Clients hunting today. Monthly starts − UC (net change) is calendar throughput and is never added up into a backlog.
This month ÷ comparison month − 1, shown only where both periods count the same way; the partial month is compared with the same days.

terms.unit: Confirmed starts with a matched form answer
terms.date: Answer given before the client's UC date
terms.source: Onboarding form 'Total out-of-pocket capital available (all-in)' (column M, live since 20 Apr 2026), matched by e-mail (form deal id as a fallback)
terms.calc: The selected range read at its upper end (the interim rule, also being carried into Jira's budget field). Up to $250K = upper end ≤ $250K; Above $250K = upper end > $250K. It measures all-in capital (down payment + closing costs + renovation + furniture + amenities), not the purchase price.

terms.unit: Confirmed starts with a matched form answer
terms.calc: Below $250K = a range ending below $250K ($150K–$200K); Range ends at $250K = $200K–$250K (a range, not an exact amount, so it is shown on its own); Above $250K = ranges from $250K–$300K up.
total_oop ≤ $225K. total_oop is recorded mostly at purchase, so it is unknown for most clients still hunting: compare speed by the onboarding budget instead.
The lead's stated minimum capital, in bands (Under $100K … $500K+). A lower bound, not the onboarding budget.

terms.unit: Confirmed starts with a matched form answer
terms.date: Answer given before the client's UC date
terms.source: Onboarding form column AA (self-reported experience submitting offers before STRSearch)
terms.calc: No offers / 1–2 / 3+.

terms.source: Derived from the issue created date
terms.calc: due = due date (created before 1 Jun 2026); created+4 = no due date; won = Pipedrive won date (created from 1 Jun 2026).
Clients are compared only with clients who started in the same month, under the same client experience and start-date rule (Mantel–Haenszel risk difference across those strata, with a 95% interval).

terms.source: 12 Nov Jira and Pipedrive extracts (e-mails, Pipedrive person id), pseudonymised
terms.calc: Won deals: deals sharing an e-mail, a Jira issue or that issue's client are one client (C####). Jira: issues sharing a Pipedrive person id or primary e-mail are one client (JC####).

terms.term: Repeat service sale / multiple searches / multiple purchases
terms.unit: Clients and their deals or issues
terms.calc: Repeat service sale = a client's 2nd or later won deal. Multiple searches = 2+ signed-up Jira issues. Multiple purchases = 2+ completed purchases (status first).

terms.source: Cash Forecast reconciliation (e-mails, Jira key typed in Pipedrive, onboarding forms, brokerage / lender / affiliate records)
terms.calc: Won deals without a Jira match in the reporting layer, resolved: own Jira issue found, separate purchase, second deal under review, repeat purchase without its own issue, closing record, or no record.

terms.unit: Signed-up clients known to have gone UC
terms.date: 12 Nov extract (data to 11 Nov) + 16 Nov statuses
terms.source: Jira Address_Fell_Out_Of_Contract, under_contract_count, first / latest UC dates
terms.calc: Documented = a fall-out address; Ended = a contract on record, no purchase, now hunting / paused / refunded / Additional Service; Back under contract = UC again after a search status; Entered twice = UC entered twice, then bought (cannot tell a new contract from a repeated entry).

terms.term: STR Cribs: selection vs verified handoff
terms.source: Jira Designer Used (selection); Cribs tracker Cribs_Data matched by property address (handoff)
terms.calc: Selection = Designer Used is STR Cribs (the recorded partner choice). Verified handoff = a Cribs deal at the purchase address in 'Handed off to PM'.

terms.source: won_clients_master + client_cash_forecast; the Cash Forecast model at its default assumptions
terms.calc: Booked value (deal value) → contract balances (assumed collected + outstanding) → expected service collections + affiliate revenue − future refunds = estimated net cash.

budget.population: won engagements with a confirmed Jira start

reasons.early: 2024 Jira records are incomplete: 73 of 88 deals won in 2024 have a Jira issue (2025: 257 of 269), so 2024 starts and contracts are undercounted.
reasons.rule: The start date rule changed on 1 Jun 2026: from June a start is the won date, before it the kickoff date (a median 5 days later), so starts from June are not counted the same way as earlier months.
reasons.ucgap: 46 of the 86 clients who closed from August to December 2025 have no Under Contract date, so the contract counts for June to November 2025 are too low.
reasons.zero: No events in the comparison period.

quality.title: Closing dates after the data date
quality.detail: property_closed_date holds dates up to 04 Dec 2026. They look like scheduled closings. client_events lists them as 'Property Closed' and the cash view counts their second split-pay installment as collected.
quality.impact: This build counts them as scheduled, not closed: they are left out of CLOSED counts, durations and attainment. Cash figures show them separately.

quality.title: Closing date on clients still Under Contract or Passed Inspection
quality.detail: The closing-date field is filled before the status moves to CLOSED (some dates are in the future).
quality.impact: CLOSED counts follow the date field, not the status.

quality.title: Under Contract = latest valid contract, not the first
quality.detail: property_uc_date is the latest currently valid UC date (falls back to the first). A contract that falls through moves or clears it; the first-contract history and contract counts are not in the reporting layer.
quality.impact: Days to UC measure time to the contract that stands today. Fall-through rates cannot be measured from this version.

quality.title: Won engagements with no Jira match
quality.detail: 3 were won in the last 60 days; the rest are older (2024: 15, 2025: 12, 2026: 20). The SQL reference notes a client may have bought a search that has not started.
quality.impact: They keep a Pipedrive fallback start date, which is not a confirmed start: they are excluded from starts, durations and cohorts but stay in won counts and the cash model.

quality.title: Jira key in Pipedrive differs from the matched issue
quality.detail: The Pipedrive deal names a different Jira key from the issue that links to it through pd_deal_id.
quality.impact: Flagged as data anomalies; counted with the pd_deal_id match.

quality.title: Won engagements whose Jira issue is still pre-sale
quality.detail: The Pipedrive deal is won but the Jira status is New Clients, Onboarding Completed or Services Declined. The reporting layer still gives them a confirmed (Jira) start: the won date.
quality.impact: They count as Client Started events and in cohorts, but not as signed, active or hunting Jira clients.

quality.title: Signed Jira clients with no won engagement
quality.detail: 14 have no deal link; the rest link to a deal that is not won or not unique. 17 signed clients have no client_start_date at all.
quality.impact: They count as signed / active / hunting Jira clients but have no engagement-grain start.

quality.title: Two hunting counts
quality.detail: The SQL reference's current hunting count is won_clients_master WHERE hunting_clients = 1 AND has_jira_match = 1; Jira issues in hunting statuses without a won engagement add the difference.
quality.impact: Status-based client counts use the Jira grain; engagement measures use the master.

quality.title: Engagements flagged has_data_anomaly
quality.detail: key mismatch: 4; UC before start: 1; hunting with a UC date: 9
quality.impact: Kept in every count (the SQL reference says never drop anomalous won deals).

quality.title: Payment type looks defaulted to Split Pay
quality.metric: Split Pay on 5,999 of 6,005 lost deals
quality.detail: pipedrive_reporting_base fills payment_type on every deal, while the raw field carried into jira_reporting_base is recorded on only 185 deals. Where both exist they agree.
quality.impact: The cash model treats every unrecorded engagement as Split Pay, so modeled outstanding balances are an upper bound if some clients paid in full.

quality.title: Abnormal values excluded from aggregates
quality.metric: 1 total_oop · 2 budget · 1 deals sent · 5 zero-value wins
quality.detail: total_oop above $20,000,000 (a placeholder value), client_budget below $1,000, total_deals_sent above 500. Zero-value won deals stay in counts.
quality.impact: Excluded from averages and bands; HENRY flags are unaffected (the placeholder is not <= $225K).

quality.title: HENRY is unknown for signed clients without total_oop
quality.detail: henry_client is 0 when total_oop is missing.
quality.impact: HENRY shares use clients with a known total_oop as the denominator.

quality.title: Refunds are a Jira status proxy
quality.detail: client_refunded = current status Refunded; the date is when the status last changed. Earlier refunds that moved on, and refunds before the Jira history, are missed.
quality.impact: Refund timing can reflect status clean-ups rather than payment dates; refund-adjusted rates drop currently refunded clients from denominators.

quality.title: UC dated before the client start
quality.detail: A UC date earlier than client_start_date.
quality.impact: Left out of duration statistics (negative days).

quality.title: Start dates set to created + 4 days
quality.detail: Issues created before 1 Jun 2026 with no due date start 4 days after creation (the reporting layer's rule).
quality.impact: Small: affects older clients only.

quality.title: The start date changes meaning on 1 Jun 2026
quality.detail: Issues created before 1 Jun 2026 start on the due date (a kickoff date after the sale); from 1 Jun 2026 the start is the Pipedrive won date. The New Client Experience itself began on 27 May 2026.
quality.impact: Durations before and after June are measured from different events; compare eras with care.

quality.title: Lead channel (utm_source) is sparse
quality.detail: The reporting base has no lead-source field like the 12 Nov PD_Source; utm_source is the only channel field.
quality.impact: Channel splits describe tagged deals only.

quality.title: Funnel flags changed meaning on 27 May 2026
quality.metric: Legacy: call booked 28%; New Client Experience: call booked 0%
quality.detail: Stage-based flags (call booked, no show, onboarding) follow different stages in the legacy and New Client Experience pipelines.
quality.impact: Compare funnel rates within one experience only.

quality.title: Only the STR Search pipeline is in the reporting base
quality.detail: Since June 2026 no-show bookings move to the SDR Setter pipeline, which is not in pipedrive_reporting_base.
quality.impact: No-show and booked-call counts after June are understated.

quality.title: Deals sent is a current cumulative total
quality.detail: total_deals_sent has no dates: there is no record of when each property was sent.
quality.impact: Early deal velocity (e.g. properties in the first 14 days) cannot be measured; long searches accumulate more deals by construction.

quality.title: Reporting date
quality.detail: Read from the views' own date arithmetic (won_clients_master refresh and client_cash_forecast query date agree).
quality.impact: Cohort maturity and elapsed days are measured to this date.

populations.old: Q1: every Jira issue with a first UC / CLOSED date; KM and Q2: signed-up Jira issues
populations.new: Q1 and KM: won engagements with a confirmed Jira start; Q2: Jira issues by reporting-layer flags
